metadata.titulo: The Tao Te Ching of Laozi (Daodejing · 道德經)
metadata.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
metadata.fuenteOficial: Wang Bi Received Text (王弼本) · English Translation by James Legge & Gia-fu Feng

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 1: El Origen del Cielo y de la Tierra (El Tao Innombrable)
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 道可道，非常道。名可名，非常名。無名天地之始；有名萬物之母。故常無，欲以觀其妙；常有，欲以觀其徼。此兩者，同出而異名，同謂之玄。玄之又玄，衆妙之門。
capitulos.foneticaLiturgica: Dào kě dào, fēicháng Dào. Míng kě míng, fēicháng míng. Wúmíng tiāndì zhī shǐ; yǒumíng wànwù zhī mǔ. Gù cháng wú, yù yǐ guān qí miào; cháng yǒu, yù yǐ guān qí jiào...

traducciones.en:
1. The Tao that can be trodden is not the enduring and unchanging Tao.
2. The name that can be named is not the enduring and unchanging name.
3. Conceived of as having no name, it is the Originator of heaven and earth; conceived of as having a name, it is the Mother of all things.
4. Always without desire, we perceive the inner mystery; always with desire, we perceive only the outer manifestations.
5. These two arise together though named differently; their depth is the profound mystery, the gateway to all wonders.

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 2: La Dualidad de las Formas y la Práctica del No-Actuar (Wu Wei)
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 天下皆知美之為美，斯惡已。皆知善之為善，斯不善已。故有無相生，難易相成，長短相較，高下相傾，音聲相和，前後相隨。是以聖人處無為之事，行不言之教；萬物作而弗始，生而弗有，為而弗恃，功成而不居。夫唯弗居，是以不去。
capitulos.foneticaLiturgica: Tiānxià jiē zhī měi zhī wéi měi, sī è yǐ. Jiē zhī shàn zhī wéi shàn, sī bùshàn yǐ. Gù yǒu wú xiāng shēng, nán yì xiāng chéng...

traducciones.en:
1. When all under heaven know beauty as beauty, ugliness appears; when all know goodness as good, evil arises.
2. Being and non-being produce each other; difficulty and ease complement each other; long and short define each other; high and low incline toward each other.
3. Therefore the sage abides in the practice of non-action (Wu Wei) and conveys teachings without words.
4. He creates without possessing, acts without relying on praise, and completes his task without clinging to merit. Because he does not cling, his achievement never leaves him.

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 3: La Quietud Interior y el Gobierno de la Paz
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 不尚賢，使民不爭；不貴難得之貨，使民不為盜；不見可欲，使民心不亂。是以聖人之治，虛其心，實其腹，弱其志，強其骨。常使民無知無欲。使夫智者不敢為也。為無為，則無不治。
capitulos.foneticaLiturgica: Bù shàng xián, shǐ mín bù zhēng; bù guì nándé zhī huò, shǐ mín bù wéi dào; bù jiàn kě yù, shǐ mín xīn bù luàn...

traducciones.en:
1. Not exalting the gifted prevents contention; not prizing rare treasures prevents theft; not displaying the desirable keeps the heart free from confusion.
2. Therefore the sage governs by emptying minds, filling bellies, weakening ambitions, and strengthening bones.
3. Practicing non-forcing action (Wu Wei), there is nothing that is not well governed.

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 4: El Manantial Inagotable del Tao
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 道沖，而用之或不盈。淵兮，似萬物之宗；湛兮，似或存。吾不知誰之子，象帝之先。
capitulos.foneticaLiturgica: Dào chōng, ér yòng zhī huò bù yíng. Yuān xī, sì wànwù zhī zōng; cuò qí ruì, jiě qí fēn...

traducciones.en:
1. The Tao is like an empty vessel, yet in being used it is never drained. How deep and unfathomable, the primal ancestor of all things!
2. It blunts all sharpness, untangles all knots, tempers its brightness, and harmonizes with the dust of the world.
3. Still and profound, it ever endures. It appears to precede the sovereign lord of creation.

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 5: El Fuelle Celestial y la Imparcialidad
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 天地不仁，以萬物為芻狗；聖人不仁，以百姓為芻狗。天地之間，其猶橐籥乎？虛而不屈，動而愈出。多言數窮，不如守中。
capitulos.foneticaLiturgica: Tiāndì bù rén, yǐ wànwù wéi chú gǒu; shèngrén bù rén, yǐ bǎixìng wéi chú gǒu...

traducciones.en:
1. Heaven and Earth are impartial, regarding all things with tranquil equanimity. The sage is impartial, embracing all beings without attachment.
2. The space between Heaven and Earth is like a celestial bellows: empty yet never collapsed, the more it moves, the more life issues forth.
3. Many words lead quickly to exhaustion; far better it is to keep to the center and guard stillness.

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 6: El Valle Misterioso y la Raíz Inmortal
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 谷神不死，是謂玄牝。玄牝之門，是謂天地根。綿綿若存，用之不勤。
capitulos.foneticaLiturgica: Gǔ shén bù sǐ, shì wèi xuán pìn. Xuán pìn zhī mén, shì wèi tiāndì gēn. Miánmián ruò cún...

traducciones.en:
1. The spirit of the valley never dies; it is called the Mystic Mother. The gateway of the Mystic Mother is the root of Heaven and Earth.
2. Continuous and subtle, it ever persists; use it as you will, it never fails or tires.

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 7: La Perennidad del Cielo y el Desinterés del Sabio
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 天長地久。天地所以能長且久者，以其不自生，故能長生。是以聖人後其身而身先；外其身而身存。非以其無私邪？故能成其私。
capitulos.foneticaLiturgica: Tiān cháng dì jiǔ. Tiāndì suǒyǐ néng cháng qiě jiǔ zhě, yǐ qí bù zì shēng, gù néng cháng shēng...

traducciones.en:
1. Heaven is enduring and Earth is everlasting. They endure because they do not live for themselves; therefore they can live long.
2. Thus the sage puts his own person behind, yet finds himself ahead; detaches from his person, yet his true self is preserved.
3. Is it not through his selflessness that his highest fulfillment is realized?

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 8: La Bondad Suprema como el Agua
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 上善若水。水善利萬物而不爭，處衆人之所惡，故幾於道。居善地，心善淵，與善仁，言善信，政善治，事善能，動善時。夫唯不爭，故無尤。
capitulos.foneticaLiturgica: Shàng shàn ruò shuǐ. Shuǐ shàn lì wànwù ér bù zhēng, chù zhòngrén zhī suǒ è, gù jǐ yú Dào...

traducciones.en:
1. The highest good is like water. Water benefits all ten thousand things without striving, settling in places that men despise; hence it is close to the Tao.
2. In dwelling, be close to the land; in heart, cultivate depth; in friendship, show kindness; in words, speak truth; in government, maintain peace; in work, show skill; in action, choose the right time.
3. Because it never contends, it is free from all fault.

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 9: La Moderación y el Retiro Oportuno
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 持而盈之，不如其已；揣而銳之，不可長保。金玉滿堂，莫之能守；富貴而驕，自遺其咎。功遂身退，天之道也。
capitulos.foneticaLiturgica: Chí ér yíng zhī, bùrú qí yǐ; chuǎi ér ruì zhī, bùkě cháng bǎo...

traducciones.en:
1. To hold and fill a cup to the brim is not as good as stopping in time; to sharpen a blade to extreme sharpness ensures it cannot long endure.
2. A hall filled with gold and jade cannot be guarded; arrogance born of wealth and honor brings about its own downfall.
3. To complete the work and quietly withdraw: this is the way of Heaven.

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 10: La Unidad del Alma y el Poder de la Virtud Secreta
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 載營魄抱一，能無離乎？專氣致柔，能如嬰兒乎？滌除玄覽，能無疵乎？愛國治民，能無為乎？天門開闔，能為雌乎？明白四達，能無知乎？生之畜之，生而弗有，為而弗恃，長而弗宰，是謂玄德。
capitulos.foneticaLiturgica: Zǎi yíng pò bào yī, néng wú lí hū? Zhuān qì zhì róu, néng rú yīng'ér hū?...

traducciones.en:
1. Embracing unity in soul and body, can you remain undivided? In gathering vital breath (Qi) and attaining softness, can you become as a newborn infant?
2. In cleansing the mystic mirror of the mind, can you leave it without a stain? In loving people and governing, can you practice non-forcing action?
3. In the opening and closing of Heaven's gates, can you abide as the receptive feminine? In illuminating all realms, can you remain free of craftiness?
4. To give life and nurture, to produce without possessing, to act without demanding praise, to lead without dominating: this is the Mysterious Virtue (Xuan De).

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 11: La Utilidad de lo No Existente y el Vacío
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 三十輻，共一轂，當其無，有車之用。埏埴以為器，當其無，有器之用。鑿戶牖以為室，當其無，有室之用。故有之以為利，無之以為用。
capitulos.foneticaLiturgica: Sānshí fú gòng yī gǔ, dāng qí wú, yǒu chē zhī yòng...

traducciones.en:
1. Thirty spokes meet in the hub of a wheel, but it is on its central hole that the use of the cart depends.
2. Clay is fashioned into vessels, but it is on their empty space that the use of the vessel depends.
3. Doors and windows are cut out to make a room, but it is on its empty space that the use of the room depends. Therefore, what is provides the advantage, but what is not provides the real usefulness.

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 12: La Moderación de los Sentidos
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 五色令人目盲；五音令人耳聾；五味令人口爽；馳騁畋獵，令人心發狂；難得之貨，令人行妨。是以聖人為腹不為目，故去彼取此。
capitulos.foneticaLiturgica: Wǔ sè lìng rén mù máng; wǔ yīn lìng rén ěr lóng; wǔ wèi lìng rén kǒu shuǎng...

traducciones.en:
1. The five colors blind the human eye; the five musical notes deafen the human ear; the five flavors dull the human palate.
2. Racing and hunting drive the mind into frenzy; rare treasures obstruct righteous conduct.
3. Therefore the sage attends to the inner belly and not to the fleeting eyes; he discards the outer and embraces the essential inner.

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 13: La Calma ante el Honor y la Desgracia
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 寵辱若驚，貴大患若身。何謂寵辱若驚？寵為下，得之若驚，失之若驚，是謂寵辱若驚。何謂貴大患若身？吾所以有大患者，為吾有身，及吾無身，吾有何患？故貴以身為天下，若可寄天下；愛以身為天下，若可託天下。
capitulos.foneticaLiturgica: Chǒng rǔ ruò jīng, guì dà huàn ruò shēn...

traducciones.en:
1. Favor and disgrace cause anxiety; great affliction is regarded like one's own body.
2. Why do favor and disgrace cause anxiety? Favor is precarious: gaining it brings fear, losing it brings fear. Why is affliction like one's body? We have afflictions because we cling to our separate self; if we have no selfish ego, what affliction can touch us?
3. He who cherishes the world as his own self can be entrusted with the world; he who loves the world as his own person can be given stewardship of all under heaven.

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 14: La Manifestación del Misterio Invisible e Inaudible
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 視之不見，名曰夷；聽之不聞，名曰希；搏之不得，名曰微。此三者不可致詰，故混而為一。其上不皦，其下不昧。繩繩不可名，復歸於無物。是謂無狀之狀，無物之象，是謂惚恍。迎之不見其首，隨之不見其後。執古之道，以御今之有。能知古始，是謂道紀。
capitulos.foneticaLiturgica: Shì zhī bù jiàn, míng yuē Yí; tīng zhī bù wén, míng yuē Xī; bó zhī bù dé, míng yuē Wēi...

traducciones.en:
1. Looked at but not seen, it is named the Invisible (Yi); listened to but not heard, it is named the Inaudible (Xi); grasped at but not caught, it is named the Impalpable (Wei).
2. These three cannot be further scrutinized; hence they blend into a single Whole. Its upper part is not bright, and its lower part is not dark.
3. Endless in its continuous operation, it cannot be named, returning ever to the realm of Non-Being. It is the form of the formless, the image of the imageless, the elusive and mysterious.
4. Meet it and you see no front; follow it and you see no back. Hold fast to the ancient Tao to manage the affairs of the present, knowing the primal beginning: this is the thread of the Tao.

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 15: Las Virtudes Prístinas de los Antiguos Maestros
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 古之善為士者，微妙玄通，深不可識。夫唯不可識，故強為之容：豫兮若冬涉川；猶兮若畏四鄰；儼兮其若客；渙兮若冰之將釋；敦兮其若樸；曠兮其若谷；混兮其若濁；孰能濁以靜之徐清？孰能安以動之徐生？保此道者，不欲盈。夫唯不盈，故能蔽而新成。
capitulos.foneticaLiturgica: Gǔ zhī shàn wéi shì zhě, wēimiào xuántōng, shēn bùkě shí...

traducciones.en:
1. The skillful masters of antiquity were subtle, mysterious, and profoundly discerning, too deep to be fully understood.
2. Because they were unfathomable, we can only describe their appearance: cautious, like men crossing a winter stream; watchful, as if surrounded by perils; dignified, as if paying a formal visit.
3. Yielding, like ice beginning to melt; simple, like uncarved wood; receptive, like an expansive valley; quiet, like calm waters.
4. Who can make the muddy water clear? Let it settle in stillness, and it becomes pure. Who can bring tranquility into active life? Let it move gently, and it blossoms. Those who hold the Tao do not seek fullness, and being unfilled, they remain ever renewed.

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 16: El Retorno a la Raíz y la Quietud Eterna
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 致虛極，守靜篤。萬物並作，吾以觀復。夫物芸芸，各復歸其根。歸根曰靜，靜曰復命。復命曰常，知常曰明。不知常，妄作凶。知常容，容乃公，公乃全，全乃天，天乃道，道乃久，沒身不殆。
capitulos.foneticaLiturgica: Zhì xū jí, shǒu jìng dǔ. Wànwù bìng zuò, wú yǐ guān fù...

traducciones.en:
1. Attain the utmost emptiness; hold steadfast to stillness.
2. All things flourish together, and I watch them return to their origin. Countless beings spring forth, and each returns to its primal root. Returning to the root is called stillness; stillness is called fulfilling one's destiny.
3. To know the eternal is enlightenment; to ignore the eternal is to act blindly and court disaster. Knowing the eternal leads to tolerance, impartiality, nobility, oneness with Heaven, and unity with the Tao. Everlasting, one faces no peril even in death.

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 17: El Arte Supremo del Gobierno Invisible
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 太上，不知有之；其次，親而譽之；其次，畏之；其次，侮之。信不足焉，有不信焉。悠兮其貴言。功成事遂，百姓皆謂：我自然。
capitulos.foneticaLiturgica: Tài shàng, bù zhī yǒu zhī; qícì, qīn ér yù zhī; qícì, wèi zhī; qícì, wǔ zhī...

traducciones.en:
1. With the greatest rulers, the people scarcely know that they exist. Next come those whom they love and praise. Next come those whom they fear. Next come those whom they despise.
2. When trust is insufficient, there will be no trust in return.
3. How valued are the sage ruler's words! When the work is accomplished and affairs succeed, all the people say: 'We did it naturally ourselves.

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 18: La Decadencia de la Gran Vía y el Artificio
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 大道廢，有仁義；智慧出，有大偽；六親不和，有孝慈；國家昏亂，有忠臣。
capitulos.foneticaLiturgica: Dà Dào fèi, yǒu rényì; zhìhuì chū, yǒu dà wěi; liùqīn bù hé, yǒu xiàocí; guójiā hūnluàn, yǒu zhōngchén.

traducciones.en:
1. When the Great Tao falls into disuse, benevolence and righteousness appear. When worldly cleverness arises, great hypocrisy emerges.
2. When family harmony fails, filial piety and maternal affection are demanded; when the state falls into turmoil, loyal ministers are celebrated.

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 19: El Retorno a la Sencillez y la Pureza
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 絕聖棄智，民利百倍；絕仁棄義，民復孝慈；絕巧棄利，盜賊無有。此三者以為文，不足。故令有所屬：見素抱樸，少私寡欲，絕學無憂。
capitulos.foneticaLiturgica: Jué shèng qì zhì, mín lì bǎi bèi; jué rén qì yì, mín fù xiàocí...

traducciones.en:
1. Discard pretension of sanctity and cleverness, and the people will benefit a hundredfold; discard forced morality, and the people will return to natural love; discard greed and profit, and thieves will vanish.
2. These three assertions are mere adornments and insufficient in themselves.
3. Therefore let people hold to what is genuine: display plainness, embrace simplicity, reduce selfishness, and restrain desires.

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 20: El Sabio en Aparente Soledad y Diferencia
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 唯之與阿，相去幾何？美之與惡，相去若何？人之所畏，不可不畏。荒兮，其未央哉！衆人熙熙，如享太牢，如春登臺。我獨泊兮，其未兆；沌沌兮，如嬰兒之未孩；儽儽兮，若無所歸。衆人皆有餘，而我獨若遺。我愚人之心也哉！俗人昭昭，我獨昏昏。俗人察察，我獨悶悶。澹兮其若海，飂兮若無止。衆人皆有以，而我獨頑且鄙。我獨異於人，而貴食母。
capitulos.foneticaLiturgica: Jué xué wú yōu. Wéi zhī yǔ ē, xiāng qù jǐ hé? Měi zhī yǔ è, xiāng qù ruò hé?...

traducciones.en:
1. Cease from superficial learning and be free from sorrow. What difference is there between yes and no? What difference between good and evil?
2. The multitude are joyous and celebratory, as if enjoying a great feast or ascending a terrace in spring. I alone am still and undisturbed, like a newborn infant before it has learned to smile, adrift as if without a home.
3. All men have plenty, while I alone seem to lack. My mind is simple and tranquil. Worldly men are bright and assertive; I alone am quiet and reserved.
4. Vast as the ocean, wandering as the boundless wind. All men have their active pursuits; I alone appear unhurried. I differ from other men because I prize seeking nourishment from the Mother of all life.

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 21: El Corazón del Tao y la Esencia Verdadera
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 孔德之容，唯道是從。道之為物，唯恍唯惚。惚兮恍兮，其中有象；恍兮惚兮，其中有物。窈兮冥兮，其中有精；其精甚真，其中有信。自古及今，其名不去，以閱衆甫。吾何以知衆甫之狀哉？以此。
capitulos.foneticaLiturgica: Kǒng dé zhī róng, wéi Dào shì cóng. Dào zhī wéi wù, wéi huǎng wéi hū...

traducciones.en:
1. The grandest forms of active virtue flow from the Tao alone.
2. The Tao as an entity is elusive and unfathomable. Elusive and unfathomable, yet within it are forms; shadowy and dark, yet within it is vital essence.
3. From ancient times until now, its Name has never passed away; by it we perceive the origin of all creation.

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 22: La Plenitud en la Humildad y la Entrega
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 曲則全，枉則直，窪則盈，敝則新，少則得，多則惑。是以聖人抱一為天下式。不自見，故明；不自是，故彰；不自伐，故有功；不自矜，故長。夫唯不爭，故天下莫能與之爭。古之所謂曲則全者，豈虛言哉！誠全而歸之。
capitulos.foneticaLiturgica: Qū zé quán, wǎng zé zhí, wā zé yíng, bì zé xīn...

traducciones.en:
1. Yield and you will become whole; bend and you will be straightened; be hollow and you will be filled; be worn out and you will be renewed.
2. Therefore the sage embraces the One as the pattern for the world. He does not show off, therefore he shines; he does not justify himself, therefore he is honored; he does not boast, therefore his merit is recognized; he is not proud, therefore he endures.
3. Because he contends with no one, no one in the world can contend with him.

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 23: La Moderación en las Palabras y la Unión con el Tao
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 希言自然。故飄風不終朝，驟雨不終日。孰為此者？天地。天地尚不能久，而況於人乎？故從事於道者，同於道；德者，同於德；失者，同於失。同於道者，道亦樂得之；同於德者，德亦樂得之；同於失者，失亦樂得之。信不足焉，有不信焉。
capitulos.foneticaLiturgica: Xī yán zìrán. Gù piāofēng bù zhōng zhāo, zhòuyǔ bù zhōng rì...

traducciones.en:
1. To speak little is natural. A fierce wind does not last all morning; a torrential rain does not last all day.
2. Who produces these? Heaven and Earth. If even Heaven and Earth cannot make extremes endure, how much less can man?
3. He who conforms to the Tao is joyfully welcomed by the Tao; he who conforms to Virtue is welcomed by Virtue. Trust deeply in universal harmony.

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 24: La Vana Ostentación y el Orgullo Inútil
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 企者不立；跨者不行；自見者不明；自是者不彰；自伐者無功；自矜者不長。其在道也，曰：餘食贅形。物或惡之，故有道者不處。
capitulos.foneticaLiturgica: Qǐ zhě bù lì; kuà zhě bù xíng; zì jiàn zhě bù míng...

traducciones.en:
1. He who stands on tiptoe cannot stand firm; he who strides with wide steps cannot walk far.
2. He who displays himself does not shine; he who justifies himself is not enlightened; he who boasts has no true merit; he who is arrogant cannot endure.
3. From the standpoint of the Tao, these are like remnants of food and ugly excrescences. Therefore the follower of the Tao avoids them.

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 25: La Grandeza del Cosmos y la Matriz Primordial
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 有物混成，先天地生。寂兮寥兮，獨立而不改，周行而不殆，可以為天地母。吾不知其名，強字之曰道，強為之名曰大。大曰逝，逝曰遠，遠曰反。故道大，天大，地大，人亦大。域中有四大，而人居其一焉。人法地，地法天，天法道，道法自然。
capitulos.foneticaLiturgica: Yǒu wù hùnchéng, xiān tiāndì shēng. Jì xī liáo xī, dúlì ér bù gǎi...

traducciones.en:
1. There was something formless yet complete, born before Heaven and Earth.
2. Silent and void, standing alone and unchanging, operating everywhere without exhaustion, it may be regarded as the Mother of the world. I do not know its name; I call it the Tao. If forced to describe it, I call it Great.
3. Being great, it flows; flowing, it extends far; extending far, it returns to the source.
4. Therefore the Tao is great, Heaven is great, Earth is great, and humanity is great. Man conforms to Earth; Earth conforms to Heaven; Heaven conforms to the Tao; and the Tao conforms to nature (Ziran).

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 26: La Gravedad como Raíz de la Ligereza
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 重為輕根，靜為躁君。是以君子終日行不離輜重。雖有榮觀，燕處超然。奈何萬乘之主，而以身輕天下？輕則失根，躁則失君。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 26:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 26:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 26:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 27: La Destreza Sublime sin Dejar Huella
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 善行無轍跡，善言無瑕謫；善數不用籌策；善閉無關楗而不可開，善結無繩約而不可解。是以聖人常善救人，故無棄人；常善救物，故無棄物。是謂襲明。故善人者，不善人之師；不善人者，善人之資。不貴其師，不愛其資，雖智大迷，是謂要妙。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 27:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 27:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 27:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 28: Retornar a la Condición del Infante y del Valle
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 知其雄，守其雌，為天下谿。為天下谿，恆德不離，復歸於嬰兒。知其白，守其黑，為天下式。為天下式，恆德不忒，復歸於無極。知其榮，守其辱，為天下谷。為天下谷，恆德乃足，復歸於樸。樸散則為器，聖人用之，則為官長，故大制不割。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 28:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 28:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 28:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 29: El Cuidado Sagrado del Universo sin Tratar de Forzarlo
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 將欲取天下而為之，吾見其不得已。天下神器，不可為也，不可執也。為者敗之，執者失之。是以聖人無為，故無敗；無執，故無失。夫物或行或隨；或噓或吹；或強或羸；或載或隳。是以聖人去甚，去奢，去泰。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 29:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 29:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 29:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 30: La Advertencia contra el Uso de la Fuerza y la Violencia
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 以道佐人主者，不以兵強天下。其事好還。師之所處，荊棘生焉。大軍之後，必有兇年。善有果而已，不敢以取強。果而勿矜，果而勿伐，果而勿驕。果而不得已，果而勿強。物壯則老，是謂不道，不道早已。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 30:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 30:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 30:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 31: Las Armas como Instrumentos de Desgracia
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 夫佳兵者，不祥之器，物或惡之，故有道者不處。君子居則貴左，用兵則貴右。兵者不祥之器，非君子之器，不得已而用之，恬淡為上。勝而不美，而美之者，是樂殺人。夫樂殺人者，則不可得志於天下矣。吉事尚左，凶事尚右。偏將軍居左，上將軍居右，言以喪禮處之。殺人之衆，以悲哀泣之，戰勝以喪禮處之。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 31:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 31:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 31:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 32: El Tao Innombrable y el Rocío Dulce de la Paz
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 道常無名、樸。雖小，天下莫能臣。侯王若能守之，萬物將自賓。天地相合，以降甘露，民莫之令而自均。始制有名，名亦既有，夫亦將知止，知止所以不殆。譬道之在天下，猶川谷之於江海。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 32:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 32:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 32:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 33: El Autoconocimiento y la Verdadera Fuerza Interior
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 知人者智，自知者明。勝人者有力，自勝者強。知足者富。強行者有志。不失其所者久。死而不亡者壽。

traducciones.en:
1. He who knows others is wise; he who knows himself is enlightened.
2. He who conquers others has physical force; he who conquers himself is truly mighty.
3. He who knows contentment is rich; he who dies without perishing attains true immortality.

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 34: La Grandeza del Tao que Nutre a Todos sin Dominar
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 大道氾兮，其可左右。萬物恃之以生而弗辭，功成而不名有。衣養萬物而弗為主，常無欲，可名於小；萬物歸焉而弗為主，可名為大。以其終不自為大，故能成其大。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 34:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 34:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 34:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 35: La Gran Imagen de Paz que Atrae al Mundo
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 執大象，天下往。往而不害，安平太。樂與餌，過客止。道之出口，淡乎其無味，視之不足見，聽之不足聞，用之不足既。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 35:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 35:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 35:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 36: La Transformación Sutil: Lo Débil Vence a lo Fuerte
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 將欲歙之，必固張之；將欲弱之，必固強之；將欲廢之，必固興之；將欲取之，必固與之。是謂微明。柔弱勝剛強。魚不可脫於淵，國之利器不可以示人。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 36:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 36:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 36:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 37: El No-Hacer que Todo lo Transforma en Armonía
capitulos.seccion: Daojing · El Libro de la Vía
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 道常無為而無不為。侯王若能守之，萬物將自化。化而欲作，吾將鎮之以無名之樸。鎮之以無名之樸，夫亦將無欲。不欲以靜，天下將自定。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 37:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 37:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 37:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 38: La Virtud Superior y el Desprendimiento
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 上德不德，是以有德；下德不失德，是以無德。上德無為而無以為；下德無為而有以為。上仁為之而無以為；上義為之而有以為。上禮為之而莫之應，則攘臂而扔之。故失道而後德，失德而後仁，失仁而後義，失義而後禮。夫禮者，忠信之薄，而亂之首。前識者，道之華，而愚之始。是以大丈夫處其厚，不居其薄；處其實，不居其華。故去彼取此。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 38:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 38:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 38:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 39: Capítulo 39: La Sabiduría del Tao y la Virtud Serena (Capítulo 39)
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 昔之得一者：天得一以清；地得一以寧；神得一以靈；谷得一以盈；萬物得一以生；侯王得一以為天下正。其致之也，謂天無以清，將恐裂；地無以寧，將恐廢；神無以靈，將恐歇；谷無以盈，將恐竭；萬物無以生，將恐滅；侯王無以正，將恐蹶。故貴以賤為本，高以下為基。是以侯王自謂孤、寡、不穀。此非以賤為本邪？非乎？故致譽無譽。是故不欲琭琭如玉，珞珞如石。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 39:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 39:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 39:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 40: El Retorno es el Movimiento del Tao
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 反者道之動；弱者道之用。天下萬物生於有，有生於無。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 40:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 40:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 40:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 41: La Escucha del Tao y la Gran Sabiduría
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 上士聞道，勤而行之；中士聞道，若存若亡；下士聞道，大笑之。不笑不足以為道。故建言有之：明道若昧；進道若退；夷道若纇；上德若谷；大白若辱；廣德若不足；建德若偷；質真若渝；大方無隅；大器晚成；大音希聲；大象無形；道隱無名。夫唯道，善貸且成。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 41:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 41:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 41:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 42: El Uno Engendra el Dos, el Dos Engendra el Tres
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 道生一，一生二，二生三，三生萬物。萬物負陰而抱陽，沖氣以為和。人之所惡，唯孤、寡、不穀，而王公以為稱。故物或損之而益，或益之而損。人之所教，我亦教之。強梁者不得其死，吾將以為教父。

traducciones.en:
1. The Tao produced One; One produced Two; Two produced Three; and Three produced all ten thousand things.
2. All beings carry Yin on their backs and embrace Yang in their arms; by blending these vital breaths they achieve harmonious balance.
3. What men dread is to be helpless and humble, yet the sage embraces these very states to elevate his spirit.

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 43: Lo Más Blando del Mundo Penetra lo Más Duro
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 天下之至柔，馳騁天下之至堅。無有入無間，吾是以知無為之有益。不言之教，無為之益，天下希及之。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 43:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 43:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 43:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 44: La Fama, la Riqueza y el Contento Interior
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 名與身孰親？身與貨孰多？得與亡孰病？甚愛必大費；多藏必厚亡。故知足不辱，知止不殆，可以長久。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 44:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 44:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 44:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 45: La Gran Perfección que Parece Incompleta
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 大成若缺，其用不弊。大盈若沖，其用不窮。大直若屈，大巧若拙，大辯若訥。靜勝躁，寒勝熱。清靜為天下正。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 45:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 45:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 45:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 46: La Moderación de los Deseos y la Calma
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 天下有道，卻走馬以糞。天下無道，戎馬生於郊。禍莫大於不知足；咎莫大於欲得。故知足之足，常足矣。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 46:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 46:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 46:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 47: Conocer el Mundo sin Traspasar la Puerta
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 不出戶，知天下；不窺牖，見天道。其出彌遠，其知彌少。是以聖人不行而知，不見而名，不為而成。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 47:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 47:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 47:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 48: Disminuir Día a Día hasta el No-Actuar
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 為學日益，為道日損。損之又損，以至於無為。無為而無不為。取天下常以無事，及其有事，不足以取天下。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 48:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 48:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 48:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 49: El Corazón del Sabio y la Bondad sin Distinción
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 聖人常無心，以百姓心為心。善者，吾善之；不善者，吾亦善之；德善。信者，吾信之；不信者，吾亦信之；德信。聖人在天下，歙歙焉，為天下渾其心，百姓皆注其耳目，聖人皆孩之。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 49:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 49:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 49:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 50: El Cultivo de la Vida y la Serenidad ante la Muerte
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 出生入死。生之徒，十有三；死之徒，十有三；人之生，動之於死地，亦十有三。夫何故？以其生生之厚。蓋聞善攝生者，陸行不遇兕虎，入軍不被甲兵；兕無所投其角，虎無所措其爪，兵無所容其刃。夫何故？以其無死地。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 50:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 50:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 50:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 51: La Nutrición del Tao y la Virtud Misteriosa
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 道生之，德畜之，物形之，勢成之。是以萬物莫不尊道而貴德。道之尊，德之貴，夫莫之命而常自然。故道生之，德畜之；長之育之；亭之毒之；養之覆之。生而弗有，為而弗恃，長而弗宰。是謂玄德。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 51:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 51:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 51:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 52: El Retorno a la Madre y la Preservación de la Luz
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 天下有始，以為天下母。既得其母，以知其子，復守其母，沒身不殆。塞其兌，閉其門，終身不勤。開其兌，濟其事，終身不救。見小曰明，守柔曰強。用其光，復歸其明，無遺身殃；是為習常。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 52:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 52:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 52:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 53: El Sendero Luminoso del Tao y el Rechazo a la Vanidad
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 使我介然有知，行於大道，唯施是畏。大道甚夷，而人好徑。朝甚除，田甚蕪，倉甚虛；服文綵，帶利劍，厭飲食，財貨有餘；是為盜夸。非道也哉！

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 53:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 53:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 53:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 54: El Cultivo de la Virtud en uno Mismo, en el Hogar y en el Mundo
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 善建者不拔，善抱者不脫，子孫以祭祀不輟。修之於身，其德乃真；修之於家，其德乃餘；修之於鄉，其德乃長；修之於邦，其德乃豐；修之於天下，其德乃普。故以身觀身，以家觀家，以鄉觀鄉，以邦觀邦，以天下觀天下。吾何以知天下然哉？以此。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 54:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 54:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 54:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 55: La Plenitud Vital del Recién Nacido
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 含德之厚，比於赤子。毒蟲不螫，猛獸不據，攫鳥不搏。骨弱筋柔而握固。未知牝牡之合而朘作，精之至也。終日號而嗌不嗄，和之至也。知和曰常，知常曰明。益生曰祥。心使氣曰強。物壯則老，謂之不道，不道早已。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 55:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 55:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 55:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 56: Quien Sabe no Habla; Quien Habla no Sabe
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 知者不言，言者不知。塞其兌，閉其門，挫其銳，解其紛，和其光，同其塵，是謂玄同。故不可得而親，不可得而疏；不可得而利，不可得而害；不可得而貴，不可得而賤。故為天下貴。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 56:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 56:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 56:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 57: Gobernar con Rectitud y Vivir con Libertad Espontánea
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 以正治國，以奇用兵，以無事取天下。吾何以知其然哉？以此：天下多忌諱，而民彌貧；人多利器，國家滋昏；人多伎巧，奇物滋起；法令滋彰，盜賊多有。故聖人云：我無為，而民自化；我好靜，而民自正；我無事，而民自富；我無欲，而民自樸。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 57:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 57:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 57:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 58: La Paciencia Benévola y la Moderación Serena
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 其政悶悶，其民淳淳；其政察察，其民缺缺。是以聖人方而不割，廉而不劌，直而不肆，光而不燿。禍兮福之所倚，福兮禍之所伏。孰知其極？其無正也。正復為奇，善復為妖。人之迷，其日固久。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 58:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 58:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 58:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 59: La Moderación y el Enraizamiento Profundo
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 治人事天，莫若嗇。夫唯嗇，是謂早服；早服謂之重積德；重積德則無不克；無不克則莫知其極；莫知其極，可以有國；有國之母，可以長久；是謂深根固柢，長生久視之道。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 59:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 59:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 59:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 60: Gobernar con Delicadeza como Cocinar un Pescadillo
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 治大國，若烹小鮮。以道莅天下，其鬼不神；非其鬼不神，其神不傷人；非其神不傷人，聖人亦不傷人。夫兩不相傷，故德交歸焉。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 60:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 60:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 60:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 61: La Humildad del Valle en las Grandes Naciones
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 大邦者下流，天下之牝，天下之交也。牝常以靜勝牡，以靜為下。故大邦以下小邦，則取小邦；小邦以下大邦，則取大邦。故或下以取，或下而取。大邦不過欲兼畜人，小邦不過欲入事人。夫兩者各得所欲，大者宜為下。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 61:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 61:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 61:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 62: El Tao como el Tesoro y Santuario de Todos los Seres
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 道者萬物之奧。善人之寶，不善人之所保。美言可以市尊，美行可以加人。人之不善，何棄之有？故立天子，置三公，雖有拱璧以先駟馬，不如坐進此道。古之所以貴此道者何？不曰：求以得，有罪以免邪？故為天下貴。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 62:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 62:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 62:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 63: Comenzar lo Difícil por lo Fácil
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 為無為，事無事，味無味。大小多少，報怨以德。圖難於其易，為大於其細；天下難事，必作於易，天下大事，必作於細。是以聖人終不為大，故能成其大。夫輕諾必寡信，多易必多難。是以聖人猶難之，故終無難矣。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 63:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 63:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 63:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 64: Un Árbol Gigante Nace de una Pequeña Semilla
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 其安易持，其未兆易謀。其脆易泮，其微易散。為之於未有，治之於未亂。合抱之木，生於毫末；九層之臺，起於累土；千里之行，始於足下。為者敗之，執者失之。是以聖人無為故無敗，無執故無失。民之從事，常於幾成而敗之。慎終如始，則無敗事。是以聖人欲不欲，不貴難得之貨；學不學，復衆人之所過，以輔萬物之自然，而不敢為。

traducciones.en:
1. A tree as broad as a man's embrace springs from a tiny sprout.
2. A terrace nine stories high rises from a basket of earth; a journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.
3. He who rushes into action ruins his work; he who grasps loses his hold. The sage attends to the end as carefully as to the beginning, and thus leaves nothing spoiled.

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 65: La Sabiduría Prístina de la Simplicidad
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 古之善為道者，非以明民，將以愚之。民之難治，以其智多。故以智治國，國之賊；不以智治國，國之福。知此兩者亦稽式。常知稽式，是謂玄德。玄德深矣，遠矣，與物反矣，然後乃至大順。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 65:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 65:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 65:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 66: El Mar como Rey de los Cien Ríos por su Humildad
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 江海所以能為百谷王者，以其善下之，故能為百谷王。是以聖人欲上民，必以言下之；欲先民，必以身後之。是以聖人處上而民不重，處前而民不害。是以天下樂推而不厭。以其不爭，故天下莫能與之爭。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 66:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 66:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 66:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 67: Los Tres Tesoros: Compasión, Frugalidad y Humildad
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 天下皆謂我道大，似不肖。夫唯大，故似不肖。若肖，久矣其細也夫！我有三寶，持而保之。一曰慈，二曰儉，三曰不敢為天下先。慈故能勇；儉故能廣；不敢為天下先，故能成器長。今舍慈且勇；舍儉且廣；舍後且先；死矣！夫慈以戰則勝，以守則固。天將救之，以慈衛之。

traducciones.en:
1. All the world says that my Tao is great, but seems unconventional. It is great precisely because it resembles nothing ordinary.
2. I have Three Treasures that I hold and prize: the first is Compassion; the second is Frugality; the third is Humility (daring not to put oneself ahead of others).
3. From compassion comes true courage; from frugality comes broad generosity; from humility comes leadership of the world.
4. Compassion in attack brings victory; compassion in defense brings safety. Heaven shelters and saves through the power of love.

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 68: El Arte del Guerrero Pacífico y la No-Violencia
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 善為士者，不武；善戰者，不怒；善勝敵者，不與；善用人者，為之下。是謂不爭之德，是謂用人之力，是謂配天古之極。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 68:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 68:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 68:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 69: La Estrategia de la Paciencia y el Respeto al Prójimo
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 用兵有言：吾不敢為主，而為客；不敢進寸，而退尺。是謂行無行；攘無臂；扔無敵；執無兵。禍莫大於輕敵，輕敵幾喪吾寶。故抗兵相若，哀者勝矣。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 69:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 69:2)
3. Returning to the primal root, he attains imperishable stillness and spiritual serenity. (Tao Te Ching 69:3)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 70: La Sencillez Oculta del Sabio
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 吾言甚易知，甚易行。天下莫能知，莫能行。言有宗，事有君。夫唯無知，是以不我知。知我者希，則我者貴。是以聖人被褐而懷玉。

traducciones.en:
1. The sage abides in the eternal Tao and beholds the cosmic flow in perfect tranquility. (Tao Te Ching 70:1)
2. He cultivates virtue in silence, assists all beings without vanity, and seeks no personal acclaim. (Tao Te Ching 70:2)

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 71: Reconocer la Propia Ignorancia es Sabiduría
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud

capitulos.textoOriginal: 勇於敢則殺，勇於不敢則活。此兩者，或利或害。天之所惡，孰知其故？是以聖人猶難之。天之道，不爭而善勝，不言而善應，不召而自來，繟然而善謀。天網恢恢，疏而不失。

capitulos.textoOriginal: 民不畏死，奈何以死懼之？若使民常畏死，而為奇者，吾得執而殺之，孰敢？常有司殺者殺。夫代司殺者殺，是謂代大匠斲，夫代大匠斲者，希有不傷其手矣。

capitulos.textoOriginal: 民之飢，以其上食稅之多，是以飢。民之難治，以其上之有為，是以難治。民之輕死，以其上求生之厚，是以輕死。夫唯無以生為者，是賢於貴生。

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 76: La Flexibilidad de la Vida y la Rigidez de la Muerte

capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 人之生也柔弱，其死也堅強。草木之生也柔脆，其死也枯槁。故堅強者死之徒，柔弱者生之徒。是以兵強則滅，木強則折。強大處下，柔弱處上。

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 77: El Arco Celestial que Equilibra los Extremos
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 天之道，其猶張弓歟？高者抑之，下者舉之；有餘者損之，不足者補之。天之道，損有餘而補不足。人之道，則不然，損不足以奉有餘。孰能有餘以奉天下，唯有道者。是以聖人為而弗恃，功成而不居，其不欲見賢。

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 78: La Debilidad que Vence a la Fuerza como el Agua

capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 天下莫柔弱於水，而攻堅強者莫之能勝，以其無以易之。弱之勝強，柔之勝剛，天下莫不知，莫能行。是以聖人云：受國之垢，是謂社稷主；受國不祥，是為天下王。正言若反。

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 79: Cumplir la Promesa sin Exigir a los Demás

capitulos.textoOriginal: 和大怨，必有餘怨；報怨以德，安可以為善？是以聖人執左契，而不責於人。有德司契，無德司徹。天道無親，常與善人。

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 80: La Paz de la Aldea y la Vida Armoniosa
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 小國寡民。使有什伯之器而不用；使民重死而不遠徙。雖有舟輿，無所乘之，雖有甲兵，無所陳之。使民復結繩而用之。甘其食，美其服，安其居，樂其俗。鄰國相望，雞犬之聲相聞，民至老死，不相往來。

capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 81: La Verdad Serena y la Plenitud del Sabio que Da Todo sin Reservas
capitulos.seccion: Dejing · El Libro de la Virtud
capitulos.idiomaLiturgicoOriginal: Chino Clásico (文言文 · 道德經)
capitulos.textoOriginal: 信言不美，美言不信。善者不辯，辯者不善。知者不博，博者不知。聖人不積，既以為人己愈有，既以與人己愈多。天之道，利而不害；聖人之道，為而不爭。

traducciones.en:
1. Sincere words are not fine; fine words are not sincere.
2. The good man does not dispute; he who disputes is not good.
3. The wise man is not broadly learned; the broadly learned is not wise.
4. The sage does not hoard. The more he does for others, the more he has; the more he gives to others, the greater is his abundance.
5. The Way of Heaven benefits and harms not; the Way of the Sage acts without striving.
